description: Site footer with an optional WP nav menu and a copyright line. Reads a registered WP nav menu by theme location slug. Template-owned chrome (issue 223): it is rendered once by the theme, never composed. Its content and colors are set through whitelisted site options (update_site_option), NOT by composing a footer or passing props directly. The props below document the template contract; base.php maps the pp_footer_* site options onto them.

location.description: WP theme location slug for the footer nav menu.

show_logo.description: Opt-in: render the site logo in the footer. Defaults OFF so existing footers are unchanged. When true, uses the same resolution as the nav logo.

logo_text.description: Footer logo text wordmark (only when show_logo is true). Falls back to pp_site_title() when empty. TEMPLATE CONTRACT (issue 582): NOT reachable from any supported surface — base.php never passes it and a page cannot compose a footer, so it always resolves to the site title in practice. It is documented here because pp_resolve_logo() accepts it, not because you can set it. To change the wordmark, change the site title.
logo_text.conditionality_note: show_logo is true AND no logo image resolves — a boolean prop plus a negation, neither of which the clause grammar can express

logo_id.description: Media Library attachment ID for the footer logo image (NOT a URL; only when show_logo is true). Must be an image attachment; a non-image or non-existent ID is rejected when the action is validated (same rule as the pp_logo_id site option). Set via the pp_footer_logo_id site option (issue 335) so a light logo variant can serve the dark footer while pp_logo_id stays the header logo. TEMPLATE CONTRACT (issue 582): template-supplied, not page-authored — base.php maps pp_footer_logo_id onto this prop, and that site option is the surface the image-attachment rule is enforced on. Resolution: pp_footer_logo_id, then the pp_logo_id site option, then the WP custom_logo theme-mod. The fallback to pp_logo_id applies when pp_footer_logo_id is UNSET; a set-but-invalid override does not fall back, it drops to the text wordmark.
logo_id.conditionality_note: show_logo is true — a boolean-prop precondition the grammar, whose predicates cover strings, arrays and bounded values only, cannot express

logo_alt.description: Alt text for the footer logo image. Defaults to the attachment's own alt metadata, then logo_text/site title; it is never empty. TEMPLATE CONTRACT (issue 582): template-supplied, not page-authored — base.php maps the pp_logo_alt SITE OPTION onto this prop, the SAME option the header logo uses. There is deliberately no pp_footer_logo_alt: the alt describes the brand, not the asset. Consequence when the footer runs a different image via pp_footer_logo_id — a set pp_logo_alt wins over THAT attachment's own alt metadata, exactly as it does in the header. Leave pp_logo_alt unset and each attachment's own alt is used. A value that is empty OR WHITESPACE-ONLY counts as unprovided and falls through to the rest of the chain rather than rendering; a real value renders verbatim, surrounding spaces included.
logo_alt.conditionality_note: show_logo is true AND logo_id points at a real image attachment — a boolean plus a numeric-prop precondition, neither of which the clause grammar can express

blurb.description: Short brand/description line under the footer logo (issue 300). Set via the pp_footer_blurb site option. Plain text; newlines render as line breaks.

contact.description: Contact/secondary text block, e.g. an address or email (issue 300). Set via the pp_footer_contact site option. Plain text; newlines render as line breaks. Rendered inside an <address> element; recognizable email addresses become mailto: links and international phone numbers (an explicit leading +) become tel: links (issue 427). The value stays free text — text that matches neither passes through unchanged.

copyright.description: Configurable copyright line (issue 300). Set via the pp_footer_copyright site option. When empty, the footer renders the default line '© <year> <site title>. All rights reserved.'. When set, this string replaces it verbatim (include the year yourself).

menu_label.description: Optional heading above the footer nav menu (issue 335). Set via the pp_footer_menu_label site option. Plain text; empty = no heading (the unlabelled menu of issue 300).

contact_label.description: Optional heading above the contact block (issue 335). Set via the pp_footer_contact_label site option. Plain text; empty = no heading. Only rendered when contact is also set.

secondary_location.description: WP theme location slug for an optional SECOND footer nav menu column (issue 469). base.php sets this to 'footer_secondary'. The column renders ONLY when a menu is assigned to this location (has_nav_menu); an unassigned location leaves the footer byte-identical to the single-menu layout. Assign a menu with assign_menu_location / set_menu (location 'footer_secondary'). The column is a real <nav> landmark with aria-label 'Footer secondary navigation', distinct from the primary footer nav.
secondary_location.conditionality_note: a menu is actually assigned to this location — an unassigned location renders no second column at all; that is WordPress state (has_nav_menu), which the clause grammar cannot express

secondary_label.description: Optional heading above the second footer menu column (issue 469). Set via the pp_footer_secondary_label site option. Plain text; empty = a headless second column (the same headless-when-unset rule as menu_label). Only rendered when a menu is assigned to secondary_location.
secondary_label.conditionality_note: a menu is assigned to secondary_location — WordPress state (has_nav_menu), not a prop, a slot or a value, so the clause grammar cannot express it

note.description: Optional secondary line for a delimited bottom bar (issue 335). Set via the pp_footer_note site option. When NON-EMPTY, the copyright moves into its own delimited band (border-top) and this note renders opposite it; empty = the copyright renders inline exactly as issue 300 did. Plain text; newlines render as line breaks.

social.description: Optional social-icon row (issue 382). Set via the pp_footer_social site option as a JSON string: an ordered list of {network, url} objects, e.g. [{"network":"x","url":"https://x.com/acme"},{"network":"linkedin","url":"https://linkedin.com/company/acme"}]. network must be one of a CLOSED set of known networks (x, linkedin, facebook, instagram, youtube, github, tiktok, mastodon); url must be an http(s) profile URL. Renders under the brand blurb as accessible inline-SVG icon links (aria-label per link, decorative SVG) in the reserved .site-footer__social slot; colour is the `social-link` UDC role. Unknown networks, non-URL values, non-http(s) schemes, and malformed JSON are rejected when the option is validated. Empty/unset = no row (footer byte-identical). No arbitrary icon URLs or icon fonts: the network set is fixed and its glyphs ship inline.

_band.description: The <footer class="site-footer"> itself. Set the footer's background here — this is how a dark or gradient marketing footer is built.

inner.description: The footer's inner container: the width and padding of the whole footer block.

columns.description: The column row. The space between columns is design; the track geometry is structural.

brand.description: The brand column: logo or wordmark plus the blurb.

blurb.description: The short brand paragraph under the footer logo. Its `sizing.max-width` is the footer's only measure cap, and it is a `ch` value on purpose: `ch` scales with the font, so the line stays short at ANY type size instead of fixing a pixel width the next type-scale change would invalidate. The footer is a tight marketing surface, not a general builder — the blurb is a descriptor beside two or three menu columns, not body copy.

social.description: The social-icon ROW under the brand blurb: the space between icons and the row's offset from the blurb above it. The icons' own ink is `social-link`.

obligations.why: The icons are anchors INSIDE this list with their own muted colour and accent hover. No selector says so, so nothing derives it: set `social-link` and its `:hover`.

social-link.description: The social icon links. Their colour used to follow the footer link colour option; it is its own role now.

heading.description: Every optional column heading (the menu, contact and secondary labels). Its colour defaults to `currentColor`, which in the `color` property means "inherit" — so a heading follows the footer's own text colour, and setting `_band.typography.color` for a dark footer carries the headings with it. Set a colour here only when a heading should differ from the text around it.

nav-list.description: The footer menu LIST, in both the primary and secondary columns. Its `spacing.row-gap` and `spacing.column-gap` are the rhythm of a wrapping link row; the links themselves are the `link` role.

obligations.why: The paired link role named above declares its own muted colour and accent hover, so a colour set here never reaches it. Set that role and its `:hover`.

link.description: Footer menu links, in both the primary and secondary columns.

contact.description: The contact COLUMN — the optional heading plus the address block beneath it. Its type size and line-height set the column's reading rhythm; the <address> element inside it is the `address` role and the mailto:/tel: links are `address-link`.

obligations.why: The paired link role named above declares its own muted colour and accent hover, so a colour set here never reaches it. Set that role and its `:hover`.

address-link.description: The mailto: and tel: links inside the contact block.

bottom.description: The delimited bottom bar, rendered only when a footer note is set.

bottom-row.description: The row INSIDE the bottom bar, holding the copyright and the optional note. Its `spacing.gap` is what separates them when they stack on a narrow screen. The bar's own divider and padding are the `bottom` role.

note.description: The optional secondary line in the bottom bar.
